summary: A leadership change at Audi China draws attention, as multiple high-profile new models hit the market in quick succession, prices continue to fall, and competition over intelligent driving computing power and safety technology heats up.

articles.title: Audi China Leadership Shake-Up: Zhang Jun Named President, Ru Wenmo Takes Helm of Audi Sport
articles.summary: Audi China undergoes a major executive reshuffle, with Zhang Jun succeeding as president and Ru Wenmo overseeing Audi Sport, bringing a new strategist to steer the brand's China strategy.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, Audi China has completed a key leadership transition: Zhang Jun has officially assumed the role of president of Audi China, taking full charge of Audi's business operations in the country. Meanwhile, Ru Wenmo will serve as acting head of Audi Sport operations. The change comes at a critical juncture for Audi's electrification push in China. The brand currently operates through partnerships with FAW and SAIC, and is accelerating the rollout of fully electric models via platforms such as Volkswagen Anhui, with vehicles built on the PPE and PPC platforms hitting the market in succession. As the world's largest single market, China's sales performance and electrification progress directly shape Audi's global transition timeline, making the strategic direction of its China chief a closely watched issue across the industry. Zhang Jun's appointment is widely seen as Audi's bid to deploy a more localized management team to compete in China's intensely competitive new-energy vehicle market.
articles.impact: The leadership overhaul at Audi China could speed up the rollout of electric products and streamline localized decision-making, with direct implications for the competitive dynamics among Germany's premium trio — BMW, Benz and Audi — and pricing strategies in China's high-end EV segment.

articles.title: Aeolus L8+ Launches with 700 TOPS Compute Power, Priced from 129,900 Yuan
articles.summary: The Aeolus L8+ launches at 129,900 yuan and up, bringing a 700 TOPS intelligent driving platform to the 120,000-yuan segment.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, Dongfeng Aeolus has officially launched the L8+ with a starting price of 129,900 yuan. The car's biggest highlight is its intelligent driving hardware package delivering 700 TOPS of computing power, which the company calls "full-spec on board." This brings a large-compute platform previously reserved for vehicles priced above 300,000 yuan down to the 120,000-yuan bracket. Higher computing power enables stronger perception and sensor fusion, more capable urban assisted driving, and ample headroom for future OTA upgrades to urban NOA. Against the backdrop of "democratized intelligent driving," the L8+ pricing clearly targets young families and first-time buyers, seeking differentiation through advanced driver assistance features. After launch, it will compete head-on with rival plug-in hybrid and battery-electric sedans in the same price range.
articles.impact: Delivering 700 TOPS of compute at the 120,000-yuan level signals a rapid decline in advanced ADAS hardware costs, forcing competitors to follow suit and accelerating the mainstream adoption of intelligent driving technology.

articles.title: Changan Hunter K70, World's First Range-Extended Off-Road Pickup, Launched from 192,900 Yuan
articles.summary: The Changan Hunter K70 debuts at 192,900 yuan and up, combining range-extended powertrain and off-road capability to create a new pickup category.
articles.detail: As reported by NetEase Auto, Changan has officially launched the Hunter K70 at a starting price of 192,900 yuan, positioning it as the world's first range-extended off-road pickup. The vehicle combines a range-extended electric drive system with the off-road pickup form factor, preserving cargo capacity and off-road performance while addressing the high fuel consumption and urban running costs of traditional pickups. China's pickup market has long been dominated by internal combustion powertrains, with low penetration of new-energy pickups, while the off-road segment has been heating up in recent years amid the rise of outdoor camping and off-road culture. Changan's decision to enter the off-road pickup space with range-extended technology avoids the range anxiety that pure-electric pickups face on long-distance overland routes, giving the product a clear logic. After launch, it will compete in a differentiated manner against established fuel-powered off-road pickups such as the Great Wall Poer series.
articles.impact: The combination of range-extended power, off-road capability and pickup utility creates an entirely new segment, potentially spurring more domestic brands to enter the new-energy off-road pickup space and driving the pickup market toward passenger-car-like features and electrification.

articles.title: Jiayue 07 Launches from 119,800 Yuan, Nearly 20,000 Yuan Below Pre-Sale Price
articles.summary: The Jiayue 07 debuts at 119,800 yuan, roughly 20,000 yuan under its pre-sale price, signaling a clear push to trade margin for volume.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, the Jiayue 07 has officially launched with prices starting at 119,800 yuan, nearly 20,000 yuan below the previously announced pre-sale price. Such launch-day price cuts are increasingly common in today's market, reflecting the intense competition among domestic brands in the 100,000–150,000 yuan mainstream family car segment. This price band is crowded with plug-in hybrid SUVs and battery-electric sedans, and consumers are highly sensitive to pricing and features. By unveiling a better-than-expected price at launch, the Jiayue 07 aims to quickly build up its order book and capture traffic ahead of the Double 11 car-buying season. Alongside a wave of recent launches offering benefit-based or limited-time pricing, it is evident that automakers are adopting aggressive pricing to chase market share amid year-end volume targets.
articles.impact: Pricing well below pre-sale levels will further reset consumers' price expectations, intensify price competition in the mainstream family car segment, and place direct pricing pressure on direct rivals.

articles.title: Jetta M6 Launched from 79,800 Yuan with Urban NOA and 555 km Range
articles.summary: The Jetta M6 launches at 79,800 yuan and up, offering urban NOA and 555 km of range, scoring another win for low-cost intelligent driving.
articles.detail: As reported by NetEase Auto, the Jetta M6 has officially launched at a starting price of 79,800 yuan, equipped with urban NOA (Navigate on Autopilot in urban areas) and a CLTC range of 555 km. Offering urban NOA below the 80,000-yuan mark was almost unthinkable until recently, underscoring how joint-venture brands are rapidly catching up on driver assistance features. The 555 km range also covers most urban commuting and short- to medium-distance travel needs. The Jetta brand has long focused on the entry-level market, and bringing urban NOA to an 80,000-yuan vehicle is clearly aimed at consolidating young first-time buyers with a "low price plus smart driving" formula. After launch, it will go head-to-head with popular A0-segment models such as the BYD Seagull and Wuling Bingo.
articles.impact: Bringing urban NOA below 80,000 yuan will further lower the barrier to advanced intelligent driving, forcing A0-segment rivals to step up their driver assistance and range offerings.

articles.title: Volkswagen Anhui's与众09 Launches at 169,900 Yuan for Double 11 Promotion
articles.summary: Volkswagen Anhui launches the与众09 at a Double 11 promotional price starting at 169,900 yuan, accelerating its all-electric product offensive in China.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, Volkswagen Anhui has officially launched the与众09, with a Double 11 promotional price starting at 169,900 yuan. Volkswagen Anhui is a key pure-electric joint venture platform for the Volkswagen Group in China, and the与众 series carries the brand's core mission in its electrification transition. Priced between 160,000 and 200,000 yuan, the与众09 directly targets best-selling midsize electric SUVs and sedans from domestic brands. The launch of an exclusive promotional price tied to the Double 11 shopping festival shows that multinational automakers are now deeply engaged in e-commerce-driven, event-based marketing in China. Against the backdrop of an ongoing price war among domestic new-energy models, joint venture brands such as Volkswagen are seeking more flexible pricing and localized product strategies to defend their market share.
articles.impact: Volkswagen Anhui's entry into the mainstream price segment with a promotional price signals a more pragmatic and flexible electrification strategy among joint venture brands in China, intensifying competition in the 160,000–200,000 yuan EV market.

articles.title: Lu Wenmo Takes Charge of Audi Sport as High-Performance Division Sees Management Overhaul
articles.summary: Alongside the leadership change at Audi China, Lu Wenmo will oversee Audi Sport as the high-performance product line undergoes a management restructuring.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, alongside the leadership change at Audi China, Lu Wenmo will serve as acting head of Audi Sport. The division covers the RS high-performance model lineup as well as related motorsport operations and performance-car user community development. In China, high-performance models account for a relatively small share of sales but play a significant role in boosting brand value and technology image. The appointment coincides with Zhang Jun taking over as president of Audi China, indicating a systematic restructuring of Audi's management in the country. Against the backdrop of electrification, the RS lineup is also expanding into plug-in hybrid and battery-electric performance cars. Whether China will see an accelerated introduction of such models will be a key focus to watch under the new management team.
articles.impact: The reshuffling of Audi's high-performance business in China could affect the rollout pace and localized marketing of RS and other performance models, adding uncertainty to the luxury performance car segment.

articles.title: World Intelligent Connected Vehicles Conference Opens, Global Smart Mobility Race in Focus
articles.summary: The World Intelligent Connected Vehicles Conference has opened, with intelligent connectivity and vehicle-road-cloud integration drawing global industry attention.
articles.detail: According to Sina Auto, the World Intelligent Connected Vehicles Conference recently opened. As a major international industry event in the intelligent connected vehicle space, the conference focuses on cutting-edge topics such as autonomous driving, vehicle-road-cloud integration, smart cockpits, and data security, attracting automakers, parts suppliers, and tech companies from around the world. Intelligent connectivity has become the main battleground for global auto industry competition. China leads in deploying urban NOA (Navigate on Autopilot) and rolling out high-computing smart driving platforms, while Europe and the US continue to advance in regulatory approval and data compliance. The conference provides a platform for the industry to align on technology roadmaps and standards, while also offering direction for the next phase of commercialization of intelligent connected vehicles.
articles.impact: Policy and technology signals from the conference will influence regulation and the commercialization pace of intelligent connected vehicles, benefiting relevant supply chain companies and advancing global standard coordination.

articles.title: XPeng VP Calls for an End to Bashing Post-2000 Generations
articles.summary: An XPeng vice president has urged the public to stop criticizing people born after 2000, reflecting automakers' battle for young consumers.
articles.detail: According to Baidu Hot Search, an XPeng Motors vice president publicly called on public opinion to "lay off the verbal attacks on the post-2000 generation." The remarks come amid ongoing societal debate over the workplace and consumption habits of people born after 2000, and tie closely to the auto industry's push to stay youthful. This cohort is steadily becoming a key growth driver for both car purchases and industry talent: on the consumer side, they value smart cockpit features, autonomous driving and design more than previous generations; on the talent side, R&D and software teams at smart EV makers are getting younger. As a brand built around intelligent technology, XPeng's user profile and product definitions are already deeply tied to younger demographics — the executive's remarks serve as both a statement of brand positioning and a dual gesture toward young users and employees.
articles.impact: An automaker executive speaking up publicly for the younger generation highlights the post-2000 cohort's importance on both the consumption and talent fronts, potentially pushing more brands to skew younger in product positioning and employer branding.

articles.title: Shenzhen Bans Horn Honking Around the Clock with 500-Yuan Fine — What About Self-Driving Cars That Honk Automatically?
articles.summary: Shenzhen has banned motor vehicle horn honking 24/7, with violations carrying a 500-yuan fine, raising new debate over autonomous driving systems that sound horns automatically.
articles.detail: According to Sogou News, Shenzhen has implemented a round-the-clock ban on motor vehicle horn honking, with violators facing a 500-yuan fine. One practical issue raised by the new rule is that a growing number of intelligent vehicles are equipped with automatic horn alerts — for example, a short honk triggered when pedestrians, non-motorized vehicles or potential collision risks are detected. In no-horn zones, how such system-triggered honking should be treated and how liability should be assigned remains unclear, as detailed rules have yet to be issued. In addition, features such as sentry mode and remote warning sounds on some models could also trigger horns. This policy conflict exposes the lag in aligning traffic regulations with intelligent driving capabilities, requiring automakers to adapt sound strategies by region and regulators to provide clear definitions.
articles.impact: The clash between the no-horn rule and automatic honking in smart driving systems will push automakers to optimize region-specific sound strategies and drive the refinement and improvement of traffic regulations for connected and intelligent vehicles.

articles.title: A Big Year for Flagship SUVs: BYD Sea Lion 08 and Lynk & Co 900L Ready to Launch
articles.summary: BYD releases official images of the Sea Lion 08, while a seven-seat version of the Lynk & Co 900L is spotted — the flagship SUV race is heating up.
articles.detail: According to NetEase Auto, BYD's upcoming flagship SUV, the Sea Lion 08 (part of the automaker's No. 8 series), is set to debut soon, featuring a redesigned exterior shaped by user feedback and a more luxurious cabin. Meanwhile, the Lynk & Co 900L has been spotted with a seven-seat configuration, extended driving range, and optional two-tone body paint and disc-style wheels. Both models target the mid-to-large SUV segment, a fiercely contested space already dominated by strong players such as Li Auto, AITO and NIO. The Sea Lion 08 carries BYD's ambition to elevate its brand, while the Lynk & Co 900L leverages its seven-seat layout and design options to attract family buyers. With multiple automakers launching new models in rapid succession, the mid-to-large SUV market is set to enter a new arms race across cabin space, intelligent driving and premium features.
articles.impact: BYD's and Lynk & Co's flagship SUV push will intensify competition in the mid-to-large SUV segment, making seven seats, long range and personalized options new battlegrounds in the premium SUV market.

articles.title: Safety Shouldn't Be Tiered: After AI-Driving Parity, Safety Parity Becomes the Next Frontier
articles.summary: Changan vows to democratize safety tech across all trims, while 700TOPS of computing power reaches the mass market — the safety parity trend is emerging.
articles.detail: In an interview reported by NetEase Auto, Changan Automobile executive Jiang Ping stated that "safety should not be tiered by trim level," pledging to make advanced safety technology accessible across more models. Around the same time, the newly launched Aeolus L8+ brought 700TOPS of computing power to the 129,900-yuan price range. Both developments point to the same trend: after the democratization of intelligent driving and computing power, the broad accessibility of safety technology is becoming the industry's next competitive focus. Passive and active safety features have long been segmented by price tier, with entry-level trims often criticized for insufficient safety redundancy. As competition intensifies and consumer safety awareness grows, making advanced safety capabilities standard equipment will become both a brand-reputation imperative and a compliance requirement. Regulators including the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology are also tightening oversight of intelligent connected vehicle safety.
articles.impact: The democratization of safety technology will become a new differentiator for automakers, driving the adoption of safety features as standard across entire model lineups, raising industry entry barriers, and benefiting suppliers of safety software and hardware.
